sources.locator: Official ASNEF.FIN.DAT; complete transient scan of 9,200,232 fixed-width records; four strict private-identifier and name matches; identifiers withheld
sources.collection_name: World War II Army Enlistment Records
sources.rights_notes: No raw row or full private identifier is retained. Thomas J Daughtry's printed value was ineligible for the strict eight-digit comparison and a name-only hit was not assigned. The incomplete file is not a comprehensive OSS, officer, Navy, Marine Corps, civilian, WAC, Coast Guard, or foreign roster; a non-hit is not negative proof. Dominick Dattoma's occupation value 993 is not interpreted because the official table does not define 9-93.

sources.title: World War II Army Enlistment Records: Code Lists
sources.repository_publisher: National Archives at College Park - Electronic Records
sources.locator: Civilian-occupation entries 1-34, 1-75, and 7-38 visually checked on PDF physical pages 190, 191, and 283; summary table checked on physical page 171
sources.collection_name: World War II Army Enlistment Records technical documentation
sources.rights_notes: Historical occupation codes identify neither a specific employer nor the sequence from Army service to OSS. Value 993 is left uninterpreted because 9-93 is absent from the official occupation table; it is not silently converted to the separately defined 7-93 apprentice category.

affiliations.date_precision: Civilian-occupation value 134 was recorded at Army entry on September 11, 1943. NARA's code table defines 1-34 as shipping and receiving clerks; no employer, industry, or location is identified.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier confirms the Army identity. The historical occupation code does not name an employer and is not expanded to a company, warehouse, railroad, port, or government agency.

affiliations.date_precision: Civilian-occupation value 175 was recorded at Army entry on September 25, 1943. NARA's code table defines 1-75 as salespersons; no employer, product, industry, or location is identified.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier confirms the Army identity. No employer, sales specialty, or namesake biography is inferred from the broad historical code.

affiliations.date_precision: Civilian-occupation value 738 was recorded at Army entry on March 10, 1942. NARA's code table defines 7-38 as brakemen, railroad; no railroad company, route, or location is identified.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier confirms the Army identity. The occupation is not attributed to the Long Island Rail Road or any other carrier without documentary evidence.
